about: The Sky Devotion: a short devotion chosen each day by what the sky is doing. Written by La Porte Weather Now (laporteweathernow.com). Scripture: King James Version (public domain), each verse checked against two independent KJV texts. Free to share with credit.

entries.kjv: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
entries.text: Clear skies make it easy to see the day as a gift. The psalmist didn't wait for a perfect week to rejoice; he rejoiced in the day he was given. Name three good things before lunch, and thank God for each one.

entries.kjv: The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.
entries.text: A clear sky is a sermon without words. Every sunrise says the same thing: Someone made this, and made it beautiful. Step outside for one minute today, look up, and say thank you.

entries.kjv: It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
entries.text: This morning's light is new, and so is God's mercy. Yesterday's mistakes don't get the last word over today. Start fresh, and offer someone else the same fresh start.

entries.kjv: From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORD’s name is to be praised.
entries.text: On a clear day you can follow the sun's whole path, from first light to last. Praise fits all of it, the busy hours and the quiet ones. Pick one moment this evening to watch the light go down and give thanks.

entries.kjv: And he shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, even a morning without clouds; as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.
entries.text: David pictured a good leader as a morning without clouds: clear, warm, and good for growing things. That is how our words and work can land on the people around us. Be that kind of light for someone today.

entries.kjv: That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.
entries.text: The sun came up on everybody this morning without checking who deserved it. Jesus said that is how our Father loves, and how we should love too. Do something kind today for someone who can't pay you back.

entries.kjv: For the LORD God is a sun and shield: the LORD will give grace and glory: no good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.
entries.text: The psalm calls God a sun and a shield: light to see by, and protection from what we can't see. Both are given, not earned. Walk in the light you have today, and trust Him with the rest.

entries.kjv: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
entries.text: The sun crosses the sky and the shadows shift all day, but God doesn't change like that. Every good thing in your life comes from a steady, generous Father. Thank Him today for one good gift you usually take for granted.

entries.kjv: And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.
entries.text: Some days the weather is just right, and it's hard not to call it very good. God called His creation very good long before we did. Get outside today if you can, and enjoy what He made.

entries.kjv: O LORD, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all: the earth is full of thy riches.
entries.text: On a mild, bright day the earth's riches are easy to see: trees, birds, sky, neighbors out walking. The psalmist couldn't count them all. Take a walk and count a few of God's works yourself.

entries.kjv: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage.
entries.text: A beautiful day is a good reminder of the pleasant places God has given you: a home, a town, people who know your name. Gratitude grows when we say it out loud. Tell someone today what you love about where you live.

entries.kjv: The LORD is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.
entries.text: A gentle day feels like one of God's tender mercies, and the psalm says those mercies cover everything He made: people, animals, fields and lakes. None of it is left out. Show that same care today to a person or creature near you.

entries.kjv: And now men see not the bright light which is in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.
entries.text: On a gray day the sun is still up there; we just can't see it. Job learned that God is at work even when the sky looks blank. Keep going today, trusting that the light hasn't gone anywhere.

entries.kjv: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
entries.text: Gray skies can weigh on the heart, and the psalmist knew that feeling. He talked to his own soul and pointed it back to hope. If today feels heavy, tell God honestly, then call or text someone you trust.

entries.kjv: Who is among you that feareth the LORD, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the LORD, and stay upon his God.
entries.text: Isaiah wrote to people walking without much light, and he didn't tell them to pretend. He told them to trust and lean on God. On a dim day, lean a little harder, and let someone lean on you.

entries.kjv: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.
entries.text: Clouds remind us that what we can see isn't the whole story. Paul said the unseen things last longest: faith, hope and love. Spend a few minutes today on something that will outlast the weather.

entries.kjv: Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.
entries.text: A dark, cloudy day doesn't hide anything from God. He sees as clearly through the gray as through the sunshine. Whatever you're carrying today, He already sees it, and He cares.

entries.kjv: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
entries.text: Gray days pass, and so do hard seasons. The psalmist promises that joy comes in the morning, even when the night feels long. Hold on today, and help someone else hold on too.

entries.kjv: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee.
entries.text: On a gray day, people notice anyone who brings a little light. Isaiah says God's glory has risen on His people so we can carry it to others. Be the bright spot in somebody's cloudy day.

entries.kjv: For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater: So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it.
entries.text: Rain never falls for nothing; it soaks in, and something grows. God says His word works the same way. Read a few verses today and let them soak in, even if you can't see the growth yet.

entries.kjv: Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the LORD: his going forth is prepared as the morning; and he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.
entries.text: Hosea compares God's coming to the rain: faithful, refreshing, and right on time. Farmers wait for rain they can't make themselves. Wait on God today with that same kind of hope.

entries.kjv: Who covereth the heaven with clouds, who prepareth rain for the earth, who maketh grass to grow upon the mountains.
entries.text: Today's clouds are part of a plan: rain for the earth, grass for the hills, food for the animals. God prepares good things before we know we need them. Thank Him for the rain, even if it changes your plans.

entries.kjv: Ask ye of the LORD rain in the time of the latter rain; so the LORD shall make bright clouds, and give them showers of rain, to every one grass in the field.
entries.text: Zechariah tells people to ask God for rain, about the most ordinary need there is. Nothing is too small to pray about. Bring God one ordinary need today and ask.

entries.kjv: Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.
entries.text: Farmers can't hurry the rain; they plant, wait and trust. James says to wait for the Lord with that same patience. If something in your life is moving slowly, keep doing the next right thing today.

entries.kjv: Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.
entries.text: Paul told a crowd that every rain shower is a witness to God's goodness. Rain fills rivers, fields and pantries. When you hear it on the roof today, let it remind you who provides.

entries.kjv: Thou visitest the earth, and waterest it: thou greatly enrichest it with the river of God, which is full of water: thou preparest them corn, when thou hast so provided for it.
entries.text: The psalm says God visits the earth when He waters it. A rainy day is a visit, not an interruption. Slow down a little today and notice what the rain is feeding.

entries.kjv: That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.
entries.text: Rain falls on every yard on the street, the kind neighbors' and the grumpy ones'. Jesus said our Father gives like that, and asks us to love like that. Do a good turn today for someone you find hard to love.

entries.kjv: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
entries.text: Storms that frighten us don't frighten Jesus; His friends learned that on a lake much like ours. When thunder roars, go indoors, and let His words settle your heart: Peace, be still.

entries.kjv: He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still.
entries.text: Every storm has an end, and the psalm says God is the One who brings the calm. Thunder is loud, but it isn't the last word. Stay inside while it passes, and thank Him for the quiet afterward.

entries.kjv: The voice of the LORD is upon the waters: the God of glory thundereth: the LORD is upon many waters.
entries.text: The psalmist heard thunder and thought of God's power and glory. Thunder reminds us how small we are and how great He is. When it rumbles, head indoors, and let it turn your heart to worship.

entries.kjv: For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.
entries.text: Isaiah calls God a refuge from the storm, especially for the poor and the needy. Some neighbors have less shelter than others when the weather turns. Check today on someone who might need a ride, a call, or a safe place.

entries.kjv: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.
entries.text: Jesus said a life built on His words still stands when the rain and wind hit. Storms test foundations, not paint jobs. Spend a few minutes today building on the rock: read, pray, and do what He says.

entries.kjv: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.
entries.text: When the Weather Service warns of dangerous storms, getting ready is wisdom, not fear. Proverbs praises the person who sees trouble coming and takes shelter. Know where you'll go, keep your phone charged, and check on a neighbor before it hits.

entries.kjv: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
entries.text: On a day with dangerous weather, God is a very present help, right here, not far off. Faith and safety go together. Take shelter the moment a warning comes, and pray for everyone in the storm's path.

entries.kjv: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.
entries.text: Psalm 91 is a shelter you can take anywhere, even to a basement or an inside hallway. Trusting God and heeding warnings belong together. Go to your safe place when you're told, and say this psalm while you wait.

entries.kjv: And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
entries.text: Isaiah pictures people becoming shelter for one another. On a dangerous weather day you might be someone's hiding place: a ride, a basement, a phone call. Make sure your own family is safe, then be that for someone else.

entries.kjv: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.
entries.text: Fog shows how little we can see at a time, and Paul says that's true of life, too. We know in part, but God knows us fully. Drive slow, keep your low beams on, and trust Him with what you can't see yet.

entries.kjv: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
entries.text: Morning fog is here, and then it's gone. James says our days are like that, which makes each one worth spending well. Do the kind thing today instead of saving it for later.

entries.kjv: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.
entries.text: When the sun burns off the fog, it leaves no trace. Isaiah says God clears away our sins like that. If something from the past is hanging over you, turn back to Him today; He has already made the way.

entries.kjv: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
entries.text: In fog you only need enough light for the next few steps. God's word works the same way: a lamp for your feet, not a floodlight for the whole road. Take the next faithful step today, and take it slowly.

entries.kjv: The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.
entries.text: You can't see the wind, but you can see what it moves. Jesus said the Spirit works like that in people's lives. Watch today for where God is moving, and go along with it.

entries.kjv: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
entries.text: If we wait for perfect conditions, we'll never plant anything. Even a weather watcher has to admit the Teacher is right: get on with the work when the wind blows. Do the good thing you've been putting off.

entries.kjv: He causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings for the rain; he bringeth the wind out of his treasuries.
entries.text: The psalm pictures God bringing the wind out of His storehouses. Even a blustery day comes from His hand. Tie down what might blow away, and remember who holds it all.

entries.kjv: And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.
entries.text: Elijah lived through a mighty wind, but God spoke afterward in a still small voice. Loud days make it hard to hear Him. Find a quiet minute today, away from the noise, and listen.

entries.kjv: But the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!
entries.text: The disciples marveled that even the wind obeyed Jesus. On a windy day that's worth remembering: the One who calms the wind knows your name. Bring Him whatever is blowing you around today.

entries.kjv: While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.
entries.text: The first frost of the season means the seasons are turning, just as God promised Noah they always would. His faithfulness shows up in every turn of the calendar. Bring in tender plants and pets tonight, and thank Him for the harvest that's been.

entries.kjv: He giveth snow like wool: he scattereth the hoarfrost like ashes.
entries.text: Frost on the grass is God's handiwork, scattered overnight like ashes. The first one of the season is a good nudge to get ready for winter. Check the furnace and the neighbors, and make sure outdoor animals have shelter and water that won't freeze.

entries.kjv: Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?
entries.text: God asked Job where the frost comes from, and Job had no answer. Some mornings quietly remind us that we didn't make the world. Look closely at the frost today, then thank the One who did.

entries.kjv: A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
entries.text: Frosty nights are hard on animals that live outside. Scripture says a good person looks after the life of their animals. Make sure pets and livestock have shelter, bedding and water that hasn't frozen.

entries.kjv: Thy righteousness is like the great mountains; thy judgments are a great deep: O LORD, thou preservest man and beast.
entries.text: On a frosty morning, God is still the One who keeps people and animals alive, and we get to share in that care. Cover the garden, bring the pets in, and keep an eye out for any creature that needs help.

entries.kjv: If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?
entries.text: James says warm words don't warm anybody. On a bitter cold day, faith looks like a coat, a ride, a hot meal, or a call to someone who's alone. Find one person who needs warmth today, and help.

entries.kjv: She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet.
entries.text: The woman in Proverbs wasn't afraid of winter because she had her household ready for it. Getting ready is a way of loving people. Check the coats, blankets and car kit today, and share the extras.

entries.kjv: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.
entries.text: Jesus said that when we clothe and shelter people, we do it for Him. Cold days make that need easy to see. Give a coat, support a warming center, or visit someone who's shut in today.

entries.kjv: He casteth forth his ice like morsels: who can stand before his cold? He sendeth out his word, and melteth them: he causeth his wind to blow, and the waters flow.
entries.text: The psalmist admits nobody can stand up to God's cold, then reminds us He also sends the thaw. Bitter cold doesn't last forever. Bundle up, keep trips outside short, and look forward to the melting.

entries.kjv: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
entries.text: The first snow covers everything in clean white, and God says that's what His forgiveness does. No stain is too deep for Him. Come to Him today with anything you've been carrying.

entries.kjv: For he saith to the snow, Be thou on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.
entries.text: God speaks, and the first snow falls. It's a good day to marvel like a child. Slow down on the roads, enjoy the view, and let the wonder turn into thanks.

entries.kjv: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
entries.text: David prayed to be made whiter than snow after his worst failure. Fresh snow is a picture of a fresh start. Ask God for one today, and give someone else one, too.

entries.kjv: For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater: So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it.
entries.text: Snow looks like it just sits there, but it melts slowly and feeds the ground for spring. God says His word works quietly like that. Read a little today and trust that it is doing its work.

entries.kjv: For he saith to the snow, Be thou on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength. He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.
entries.text: Elihu said snow stops people's work so they can notice God's work. A snowy day slows everything down, and that isn't all bad. Rest a little, look out the window, and remember who sends the snow.

entries.kjv: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
entries.text: Snow makes the whole world quieter. It's a good day to be still and remember that God is in charge. Take a few quiet minutes with Him before you pick up the shovel.

entries.kjv: Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
entries.text: Snow is heavy, and so are some neighbors' burdens. Shoveling a walk for someone older or sick is the law of Christ with a shovel in hand. Clear a path for someone today.

entries.kjv: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
entries.text: Fresh snow covers every mark on the ground, and God says His forgiveness covers us like that. Nothing you bring Him is too dark to wash white. Talk to Him today about what you've been carrying.

entries.kjv: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.
entries.text: A winter storm is coming, and getting ready is wisdom. Proverbs praises people who see trouble ahead and take cover. Stock up early, stay off the roads when you're told to, and check on neighbors who live alone.

entries.kjv: And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
entries.text: Isaiah pictures people as shelter for one another, a hiding place from the wind. In a winter storm you might be that shelter: a warm room, a shoveled walk, a phone call. Keep your own family safe first, then look around.

entries.kjv: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
entries.text: When a winter storm closes the roads, home becomes a shelter. The psalmist could sleep in peace because God kept him safe. Stay put if you can, keep warm, and rest in Him tonight.

entries.kjv: He casteth forth his ice like morsels: who can stand before his cold?
entries.text: Ice is beautiful and dangerous at the same time. The psalm reminds us we can't stand against God's cold on our own. Walk carefully, drive slower, and offer a steady arm to someone who needs it.

entries.kjv: He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber.
entries.text: On icy days every step needs care. The psalm promises that God watches over us and never sleeps. Take small steps, salt your neighbor's steps too, and trust the One who keeps you.

entries.kjv: By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.
entries.text: Job's friend said frost and ice come by the breath of God, freezing the waters fast. Even a frozen world is in His hands. Be patient with slow roads today, and patient with the people on them.

entries.kjv: The LORD is thy keeper: the LORD is thy shade upon thy right hand. The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night.
entries.text: On a hot day shade is a gift, and the psalm says God Himself is our shade. Take care of your body; it's His, too. Drink water, rest in the shade, and check on older neighbors who may not have air conditioning.

entries.kjv: And there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the daytime from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm and from rain.
entries.text: Isaiah promised a shelter from the heat. Cooling centers, shade trees and a cold glass of water are small pictures of that care. Share some shade today with a person or animal who needs it.

entries.kjv: Blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD, and whose hope the LORD is. For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green; and shall not be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit.
entries.text: A tree by the river stays green in the heat because its roots reach water. Trust in God works like that in hard seasons. Drink plenty of water today, and drink deeply from His word, too.

entries.kjv: And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
entries.text: Jesus said even a cup of cold water given in His name matters. On a hot day, that cup may be the most loving thing you do. Hand a bottle of water to someone working outside, and put a bowl out for the animals.

entries.kjv: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
entries.text: After the flood, God set a rainbow in the sky as a promise to the whole earth. Storms come, but His promises stand. Look for signs of His faithfulness today, and thank Him for bringing you through.

entries.kjv: Then are they glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven.
entries.text: The quiet after a storm is its own kind of gladness. The psalm says God brings us safely to harbor. If yesterday was rough, rest today, and help a neighbor clean up.

entries.kjv: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
entries.text: Yesterday's storm is over, and cleanup days often show neighbors at their best. Paul says God works all things together for good for those who love Him. Pitch in where you can, and look for the good He's doing.

entries.kjv: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
entries.text: God promises to be with us in high water, and He also gave us sense to stay out of it. Never drive into a flooded road: turn around, don't drown. Pray for anyone facing rising water today, and keep your family on high ground.

entries.kjv: The LORD on high is mightier than the noise of many waters, yea, than the mighty waves of the sea.
entries.text: Rivers rise and roar, but God is mightier than any flood. That truth gives us peace, not permission to take chances. Stay away from fast water today, and trust Him with what you can't control.

entries.kjv: The LORD sitteth upon the flood; yea, the LORD sitteth King for ever.
entries.text: Even over a flood, God is on His throne. Floods are frightening, but they are not in charge. Follow the official warnings, help neighbors move things to higher ground, and rest in the King who reigns.
